newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS -SHORT STG VOLATILITY STEADY AT LOW LEVELS.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS -SHORT STG VOLATILITY STEADY AT LOW LEVELS.

text.p: Short sterling options volatility showed no sign of rebounding from its low levels on Tuesday amid signs British inflation is set to remain tame, traders said.
The forthcoming Bank of England (BoE) inflation report, due on Wednesday, failed to stir up nerves as analysts expected it to paint a healthy inflation picture after four rate hikes since May.
"That's why the vol hasn't really picked up," said one trader. "There is only bits and bobs trading."
The December 92.75 straddle was quoted at around 6.80-6.90 percent implied volatility. One trader said bids and offers for at-the-money strikes were between 7.50 and 8.11 percent.
December short sterling futures stood 0.02 up on the day at 92.65, down from their 92.71 spike up last week.
A leap on Tuesday in July headline inflation to 3.3 percent -- the highest in nearly two years -- was shrugged off as analysts mainly blamed it on budget duty increases and mortgage rises.
This was evident in a fall of 0.5 percent in RPIY, the measure which strips out both mortgage interest payments and indirect tax.

Junior Treasury minister Geoffrey Robinson said he expected underlying inflation to drop back to the government's target of 2.5 percent within the next couple of months. It rose to 3.0 percent in the year to July from 2.7 percent in June.
Short sterling vols were pummelled from around 8.75 percent last week, when the BoE raised official interest rates by 25 basis points to 7.0 percent, but signalled no further rises near term.
On Tuesday, the September 92.75 straddle was trading 5.50 percent mid volatility while March 92.50 was at 8.75 mid, traders said.
The session saw light call buying in September and December strikes but traders said downside puts in March seemed to be more favoured by buyers.
"Just in case the Bank of England hikes interest rates again," explained the trader.
Most active March put strikes were 92.25 and 92.50 with volatility quoted at 9.50 percent.
